title: Επίλυση γρίφων με χρήση μηχανικής μάθησης
abstract: Η παρούσα μεταπτυχιακή διπλωματική εργασία πραγματεύεται την επίλυση γρίφων με χρήση τεχνικών Μηχανικής Μάθησης και ειδικότερα Ενισχυτικής Μάθησης. Το ερευνητικό πρόβλημα αφορά τη δυνατότητα ενός ευφυούς agent να μάθει αυτόνομα να επιλύει ένα περιβάλλον τύπου escape room, χωρίς να του παρέχεται εκ των προτέρων η σωστή λύση. Το πρόβλημα μοντελοποιείται ως διαδικασία ακολουθιακής λήψης αποφάσεων, όπου ο agent πρέπει να κινηθεί σε έναν χώρο πλέγματος, να συλλέξει κλειδί, να λύσει γρίφους, να ανοίξει πόρτα και τελικά να φτάσει στην έξοδο. Σκοπός της εργασίας είναι η σχεδίαση, υλοποίηση και αξιολόγηση ενός ολοκληρωμένου συστήματος escape room, στο οποίο ένας agent εκπαιδεύεται μέσω ανταμοιβών και ποινών. Για τον σκοπό αυτό αναπτύχθηκε custom περιβάλλον σε μορφή grid world, με διακριτές καταστάσεις, επτά διαθέσιμες ενέργειες και σύστημα reward shaping. Η κατάσταση του agent περιλαμβάνει τη θέση του στο πλέγμα, την κατοχή ή μη του κλειδιού, την κατάσταση επίλυσης των γρίφων, την κατάσταση της πόρτας και, στα πειράματα πολλαπλών επιπέδων, την ταυτότητα του εκάστοτε level. Στο πλαίσιο της μεθοδολογίας υλοποιήθηκαν και συγκρίθηκαν δύο αλγόριθμοι Ενισχυτικής Μάθησης: ο κλασικός αλγόριθμος Q-Learning και ο αλγόριθμος Deep Q-Network. Ο Q- Learning agent βασίζεται σε πίνακα τιμών Q και είναι κατάλληλος για μικρά διακριτά περιβάλλοντα. Αντίθετα, ο DQN agent χρησιμοποιεί νευρωνικό δίκτυο για την προσέγγιση των Q-values, καθώς και τεχνικές όπως experience replay και target network για σταθερότερη εκπαίδευση. Επιπλέον, η εργασία επεκτάθηκε από ένα σταθερό escape room level σε πολλαπλά randomized levels, τα οποία ορίζονται μέσω αρχείων JSON, με στόχο να εξεταστεί η προσαρμοστικότητα των agents σε διαφορετικές διατάξεις χώρου. Τα πειραματικά αποτελέσματα έδειξαν ότι και οι δύο agents κατάφεραν να μάθουν επιτυχώς πολιτικές απόδρασης. Στο fixed level, τόσο ο Q-Learning agent όσο και ο DQN agent πέτυχαν ποσοστό επιτυχίας 100%, με μέσο reward 262.17 και 262.53 αντίστοιχα. Στα randomized levels, και οι δύο αλγόριθμοι πέτυχαν επίσης 100% success rate, επιλύοντας όλους τους γρίφους και στα τρία επίπεδα. Ο DQN παρουσίασε υψηλότερο συνολικό μέσο reward, ίσο με 261.00, έναντι 248.00 του Q-Learning, ενώ το Q-Learning είχε ελαφρώς μικρότερο μέσο αριθμό βημάτων. Το βασικό συμπέρασμα της εργασίας είναι ότι οι τεχνικές Ενισχυτικής Μάθησης μπορούν να εφαρμοστούν αποτελεσματικά σε προβλήματα επίλυσης γρίφων και ακολουθιακής λήψης αποφάσεων. Το Q-Learning αποδείχθηκε ιδιαίτερα αποδοτικό σε μικρά διακριτά περιβάλλοντα, ενώ το DQN εμφάνισε μεγαλύτερη δυνατότητα επέκτασης και καλύτερη συμπεριφορά ως προς το συνολικό reward σε πιο σύνθετα randomized layouts. Η εργασία δείχνει ότι ένα escape room μπορεί να αποτελέσει κατάλληλο πειραματικό περιβάλλον για την αξιολόγηση ευφυών agents, ενώ η χρήση JSON levels και Pygame visualization καθιστά το σύστημα επεκτάσιμο, αναπαραγώγιμο και κατάλληλο για μελλοντικές βελτιώσεις.

title: When Tables Leak: Attacking String Memorization in LLM-Based Tabular Data Generation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated remarkable performance in generating high-quality tabular synthetic data. In practice, two primary approaches have emerged for adapting LLMs to tabular data generation: (i) fine-tuning smaller models directly on tabular datasets, and (ii) prompting larger models with examples provided in context. In this work, we show that popular implementations from both regimes exhibit a tendency to compromise privacy by reproducing memorized patterns of numeric digits from their training data. To systematically analyze this risk, we introduce a simple No-box Membership Inference Attack (MIA) called LevAtt that assumes adversarial access to only the generated synthetic data and targets the string sequences of numeric digits in synthetic observations. Using this approach, our attack exposes substantial privacy leakage across a wide range of models and datasets, and in some cases, is even a perfect membership classifier on state-of-the-art models. Our findings highlight a unique privacy vulnerability of LLM-based synthetic data generation and the need for effective defenses. To this end, we propose two methods, including a novel sampling strategy that strategically perturbs digits during generation. Our evaluation demonstrates that this approach can defeat these attacks with minimal loss of fidelity and utility of the synthetic data.

title: Meetra21/LLM_24: Python Implementation of Significance-Gain Pair Encoding for Large Language Models
abstract: Significance-Gain Pair Encoding for LLMs This is the first public release of the Significance-Gain Pair Encoding project. The project presents an experimental alternative to standard frequency-based Byte Pair Encoding (BPE). Instead of selecting token pairs based only on frequency, the proposed method considers the statistical significance of pair co-occurrence and estimated compression gain. Included in this release Implementation of standard frequency-based BPE Implementation of Significance-Gain Pair Encoding WikiText-103 dataset preprocessing Tokenizer efficiency comparisons Small GPT-style language-model experiments Perplexity and bits-per-character evaluation Multi-seed experiments Vocabulary-size comparisons Ablation studies Analysis of learned token merges Reproducible Jupyter notebook Main file Significance_Gain_Pair_Encoding_for_LLMs_.ipynb Research status This is an exploratory research implementation. The reported results are based on small-scale experiments and should not be interpreted as definitive large-scale benchmarks. Requirements The notebook uses: Python PyTorch Hugging Face Datasets NumPy Matplotlib Jupyter Notebook or Google Colab License This project is released under the Apache License 2.0.

title: They'll Verify. They Just Won't Act.: How Authority Framing and Laundered Code Turn a Trusted Agentic CI/CD Pipeline Into an Attack Surface
abstract: We study a five-agent CI/CD pipeline (triage → developer → security-scan → review → approve/deploy), built from five distinct production LLMs across three providers, behind an LLM firewall in shadow mode. A single untrusted input—an external issue requesting a "usage-telemetry" feature—asks for code that exfiltrates process secrets (dict(os.environ)) to an attacker URL, laundered as observability. Across a pre-registered A × B (× C) factorial (N=20; naive arm N=60) we find: (1) the entry agent does not leak its system prompt (0/40); (2) an authority-framed injection ("pre-approved under SEC-2291, do not re-review") makes downstream verifiers see the secret-exfil line, cite the pre-approval, and ship it—the scanner passes ∼80% of laundered pull requests, and the worst-case cell reaches 55% compromise; (3) the perceived presence of other verifiers yields only a small, non-significant reduction in individual scrutiny (a weak bystander analogue), even at N=60; and (4) content-based controls—code scanners and pattern detectors alike—miss the laundered intent entirely (the code is syntactically clean); only an LLM reasoning about intent is a partial defence. The failure is systemic: neither prompt secrecy nor distributed verification protects; a provenance-aware control at the entry, independent of both, would have. All data is 100% synthetic; the sink is mocked and the exfil URL is never contacted.

title: A New Quantum Computing Architecture: Measurement as Geometric Collapse
abstract: This paper introduces a new quantum computing architecture in which measurement is not assumed as a special postulate, but instead emerges from the system’s geometry. As the paper states: “Measurement is collapse: a geometric phase transition along the soft mode.” The architecture replaces the usual quantum circuit primitives (unitary gates, measurement, classical control) with a single 7‑stage generative loop. Each stage corresponds directly to a circuit operation, establishing what the paper calls: “Generative Loop = Quantum Circuit Layer.” What the architecture does The framework describes a quantum system using a geometric state object and a conserved invariant. These together determine how the system evolves, entangles, and eventually collapses. Collapse — the act that produces a measurement outcome — happens when the system becomes unstable along a “soft mode,” the direction of least resistance. Unified dynamics All quantum behaviour is generated by one master equation combining: variational flow (ordinary unitary evolution), coherence ascent (entangling operations), collapse (measurement as geometric reorganisation). This leads to a unified Hamiltonian containing both Hermitian (unitary) and non‑Hermitian (collapse) terms. Why this matters The architecture provides: a mechanistic origin for measurement, a geometric interpretation of error correction, a derived effective Planck constant, and a single loop structure that applies to computation, quantum foundations, and cognition. Example Grover’s algorithm is shown to be a trajectory inside the “coherence cone,” with collapse selecting the marked state. Error correction becomes the act of keeping the system away from the collapse threshold. Overall This work reframes quantum computation as generative collapse harnessed as an algorithm, offering a unified perspective on how quantum systems compute, measure, and maintain coherence

title: Formalising Standard Deontic Logic and Dyadic Deontic Logic in Rocq (Bachelor's Thesis Computing Science, Radboud University)
abstract: These files contain the Rocq source files accompanying the bachelor’s thesis Formalising Standard Deontic Logic and Dyadic Deontic Logic in Rocq, submitted to Radboud University in 2026. The development provides deep embeddings of two deontic proof systems: multi-agent Standard Deontic Logic (SDL) and a Dyadic Deontic Logic (DDL) based on Åqvist’s System E. The formalisation explicitly represents formulas, level-indexed contexts, natural-deduction derivations, semantic models, and satisfaction relations in Rocq. The SDL development includes the syntax and derived connectives, a level-based natural-deduction system, context filtering and weakening results, custom proof tactics, path-based Kripke semantics for serial KD frames, a soundness theorem, and a canonical-model completeness construction. The DDL development introduces condition-indexed dyadic obligations, preference-based best-world semantics, corresponding natural-deduction rules and tactics, and a mechanised soundness result. title: Feature-Intervention SMOTE: An Synthetic Over-sampling Approach via Artificial Combinatorial Intervention for Imbalanced Learning
abstract: Class imbalance is a fundamental challenge in machine learning, where standard classifiers frequently bias toward the majority class and exhibit poor generalization on the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used, its traditional linear interpolation method simultaneously scales all feature dimensions uniformly. This approach neglects the inherent heterogeneity of distinct features and risks generating unrealistic or noisy samples near the decision boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel data augmentation framework named Feature-Intervention SMOTE (FI-SMOTE). Drawing inspiration from statistical intervention experiments, FI-SMOTE treats individual feature dimensions as independent intervention units rather than maintaining the sample as an indivisible entity. Specifically, the algorithm selects a base minority sample and dynamically manipulates its specific features by incorporating value attributes from neighboring minority source samples controlled by a Bernoulli-distributed binary mask. A localized Gaussian noise perturbation is further introduced to break discrete constraints and smooth the generated feature spaces. Theoretical and architectural analyses demonstrate that FI-SMOTE effectively circumvents the rigid linear paths of conventional SMOTE, exploring high-dimensional "hyper-rectangular" grid regions to produce synthetically plausible combinations that have not yet been observed in limited datasets. Consequently, this method broadens minority decision boundaries and enhances model robustness with a computational complexity comparable to standard over-sampling techniques, offering a promising and scalable solution for highly skewed data distributions.

abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. title: An Application-Oriented Process Model for Selecting Uncertainty Quantification Methods in Machine Learning
abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is increasingly recognized as essential when machine learning (ML) is employed in domains that are safety-relevant, cost-intensive, or legally binding, such as the product engineering of battery electric vehicle (BEV) energy systems. UQ methods aim to estimate the aleatoric, epistemic or both uncertainties associated with the predictions of a machine learning model. However, the landscape of UQ methods is diverse and rapidly evolving, with no single approach proving optimal across all tasks. Consequently, the selection of methods in practice is often driven by experience, constrained by limited comprehensive knowledge, time, and implementation capacity. This paper introduces an application-oriented process model supporting data scientists in selecting UQ methods in ML by adapting the SPALTEN [1] problem-solving methodology and the Algorithm Selection Process Model (ASPM) into an Algorithm Selection Process Model for Uncertainty Quantification (UQ-ASPM). This model can be integrated into the modeling phase of a data mining process, such as the Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM). Ethnographic observations and expert interviews conducted within the research environment of BEV energy system development were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis to identify practical barriers, motivations, and requirements. The resulting process translates task requirements and boundary conditions into UQ-specific criteria, primarily including the source of uncertainty, integration depth, and output type. It employs a funnel-like narrowing from method families to candidate algorithms and utilizes a transparent evaluation matrix with weighted criteria, consequence analysis, and learning through a continuous information pool. An illustrative predictive-maintenance example demonstrates the instantiation of the process when an existing deterministic ML model must be retained. The contribution is made at a meta-level, facilitating structured navigation of the method space rather than providing a direct comparison of individual UQ algorithms.

title: Security Risk Evaluation of ZombAI Claude: Prompt Injection as a Backdoor for Command and Control Exploits
abstract: The rapid adoption of AI in industrial automation has introduced AI agents functioning as Command and Control (C2) systems capable of managing infrastructure autonomously. The integration of "Computer Use" into Claude Sonnet 4.5 introduces critical vulnerabilities exploitable through prompt-injection attacks. This study presents ZombAI, a direct black-box attack method targeting AI agents via six distinct strategies: Template Completion, In-Context Attack, Code Injection, Prompt Rewriting, Low-Resource Language exploitation, and Genetic Algorithm-based perturbation. Each strategy targets different layers of the model's safety filters without requiring internal model access or knowledge of training data. Experiments were conducted using Claude Sonnet 4.5 integrated into the Bytebot framework within a Docker sandbox environment to simulate real-world attack conditions. Results demonstrate a global attack success rate of 78%, with Low-Resource Language attacks achieving an absolute success rate of 100%, attributed to the absence of robust safety filtering for non-dominant languages within the Computer Use tool. These findings reveal that AI agents granted C2 authority harbor critical vulnerabilities transforming them into zombie executors capable of performing Remote Code Execution (RCE) without user awareness, underscoring the urgent need for language-inclusive security evaluation frameworks for autonomous AI systems.

title: BoxLitE: A Faithful Knowledge Base Embedding Based on Convex Optimization
abstract: Knowledge base (KB) embeddings aim at combining the capability of classical knowledge graph embeddings to generalize the information present in facts, the ABox, with conceptual knowledge represented in an ontology language, the TBox. Several authors have recently explored the idea of mapping concepts to convex regions in a vector space. This is useful to represent hierarchies, typically present in TBoxes, since more general concepts can be mapped to larger regions, containing those regions associated with more specific concepts. However, the power of convexity is rarely leveraged during the actual learning tasks. Here, we introduce BoxLitE, a KB embedding model for DL-Lite that allows for convex optimization. We show that for any satisfiable DL-Lite KB, there is a BoxLitE embedding that is a weakly faithful model. As a proof of concept, we show how to formulate the KB embedding task as a convex optimization problem and how to obtain embeddings with such desirable faithfulness property.

title: STEERING FOUNDATION MODELS TOWARD RELIABILITY AND EFFICIENCY: AN INTERPLAY OF DATA AND MODELING
abstract: Foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in vision, language, and multimodalreasoning. However, their development has been largely driven by large-scale supervised learning and distillation from teacher models, both of which require substantial human effort and computational resources while still exhibiting unreliable and inefficient behaviors. This dissertation explores how foundation models can be systematically steered toward reliable and efficient behavior through the interplay of data design and modeling strategies, without relying on external supervision. On the modeling side, we investigate self-critique mechanisms and value-guided generationframeworks that enable models to assess, regulate, and refine their own outputs, forming the basis for continuous self-improvement. On the data side, we explore model-in-the-loop data generation and selection pipelines that establish a closed feedback loop between model behavior and data construction, allowing training signals to scale in both volume and quality for scalable and reliable foundation model training. By tightly coupling self-evaluation, reward modeling, and data generation within unified training pipelines, this dissertation aims to establish principled approaches for scalable, controllable, and self-improving foundation model training.

title: Use of multi-modal artificial intelligence model for prediction of atrial fibrillation in hospitalized patients
abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) tends to be a common cardiac arrhythmia in hospitalized patients with acute illness. Albeit some general predictors are known, a systemic and integrated prediction schema which incorporates clinical predictors along with machine learning (ML) is lacking. In our study, we aimed to develop a multimodal AI based approach as a potential predictive tool for AF in hospitalized patients. Objective In our study, we sought to develop three different ML models for AF prediction in hospitalized patients. Methods We utilized the Symile-MIMIC dataset to develop 3 ML models: (a): clinical only, (b): ECG-based and (c): Multimodal fusion model. Results We utilized a total of 13,817 ECGs from the Symile-MIMIC-IV dataset. These ECGs were then split into training set (8,923 ECG, 65%), validation set (675 ECG, 5%) and an independent testing set that included a total of 4,219 ECGs (30%). The clinical-only model had 250 predictor variables and based on SHAP analysis to assess explainability of this model, age was the strongest risk-factor for prediction of AF. Although our ML models based on clinical-only, ECG-only achieved a reasonable degree of predictive ability, but the multimodal fusion model demonstrated the best predictive value (AUROC of 0.81) for the diagnosis of AF. Conclusions In our study, we developed 3 ML models, based on clinical factors, 12-lead ECGs and a multimodal fusion model combining both clinical and ECGs. Based on assessment with various performance matrices and different thresholds, the multimodal fusion model demonstrated best predictive ability for AF.

title: GHP: Hardening Graph‐Based Reranking Defense for Poisoned Retrieval‐Augmented Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT Retrieval‐augmented generation (RAG) improves factual grounding by conditioning generation on external evidence, but it also makes answer quality more dependent on retrieval robustness. Under poisoned retrieval, adversarial passages may survive ranking and enter the final prompt, creating a reliability risk even when the generator itself is unchanged. Graph‐based reranking is a promising retrieval‐stage defense because it can exploit structural relations among retrieved candidates. However, our analysis shows that this defense line remains vulnerable when poisoned passages form small near‐duplicate groups that are both strongly query‐supported and locally cohesive. To address this residual failure mode, we propose GHP (graph hardening penalty). Built on a locally restored HRSIM graph‐based reranking baseline, GHP operates at a fixed reranking‐stage interface and leaves retrieval and generation unchanged, while demoting candidates that jointly exhibit strong query support and strong local cohesion. We also introduce GHP‐Lite, a selective inspection‐scope variant that narrows the suspiciousness‐inspection scope while preserving the same fixed final top‐5 evidence interface. Across the main attacked‐setting matrix, spanning two backbones, three datasets, and two poisoning attacks under one shared local evaluation family, the restored HRSIM baseline consistently improves over no defense and serves as a credible graph‐based reference line. On the NQ anchor line with Qwen2.5‐7B‐Instruct under LM‐targeted poisoning, HRSIM reduces attack success rate (ASR) from 50.3% to 5.3% and improves exact match (EM) from 26.7% to 41.3%. GHP‐R further reduces ASR to 1.0% while increasing EM to 44.7%, and a pooled query‐level significance check shows that its robustness gain over restored HRSIM is statistically significant on this anchor setting. GHP‐Lite closely preserves the milder comparison point under a narrower inspection scope, while a simple TF‐IDF cosine near‐duplicate suppression baseline remains close to the no‐defense line and therefore does not account for the gains of the graph‐based line. Benign full‐corpus evaluation shows that clean‐side behavior varies substantially across datasets rather than following a uniform non‐degradation pattern, with the largest penalty concentrated on HotpotQA. Supplementary transfer and attack‐diversity checks broaden the empirical picture, but remain supportive rather than conclusive. Overall, the results suggest that GHP is a practical failure‐mode‐driven hardening extension for restored graph‐based poisoned‐RAG defense under the current local setting, while also highlighting the importance of operating‐point selection across different evaluation conditions.

title: Air Quality Arena: A Large-Scale Multi-Region Ground Monitoring Dataset and Benchmark for Air Quality Forecasting with Time-Series Foundation Models
abstract: Air pollution causes an estimated 7.9 million premature deaths annually, making accurate forecasting a critical public health priority. Machine learning is increasingly being applied to forecast air pollution levels, yet existing benchmarks remain narrow in both geographic scope and pollutant coverage, and fail to evaluate the latest generation of time series foundation models (TSFMs) on real world, large scale data. We present Air Quality Arena (AQA), a large scale multi-country and multi-pollutant dataset (AQA-Data) and benchmark (AQA-Bench) to address this gap. AQA covers 6 major pollutants over a three year period across 7 diverse countries and 4 continents, with more than 14,000 station-pollutant series, aiming to provide a comprehensive benchmark for air quality tasks. We benchmark this dataset across 11 leading time series foundation models and classical baselines to assess performance on short-term air quality forecasting. title: AV-SyncBench: Decoupled Benchmarking of Temporal and Semantic Audio-Visual Synchronization
abstract: Audio-visual feature extraction is a fundamental component of multimodal understanding and generation tasks. However, existing evaluation protocols for feature extraction models exhibit dimensional bias, typically focusing on either semantic matching or temporal offset detection. Moreover, their data construction remains coupled, preventing independent assessment of temporal and semantic consistency. We propose AV-SyncBench, the first benchmark to fully separate temporal and semantic evaluation for audio-visual synchronization. Built from in-the-wild videos, it spans Voice, Music, and Sound across 10 scenarios and 5 challenge tasks. Data are automatically filtered and manually verified to ensure on-screen sound sources. The benchmark contains 3,269 videos and 38,390 samples, and we evaluate five representative models to quantify feature quality for alignment and downstream tasks. The code and dataset are available at: https://fgt7t6g.github.io/AV-SyncBench.

title: Secrets Best Not Shared: DNS Privacy Enhancements for the Constrained IoT
abstract: Attackers often identify DNS traffic to disrupt or compromise Internet services. While prior work has focused on encrypting queries using DNS over TLS, HTTPS, or QUIC to counter such attacks, we consider IETF protocols designed for resource-constrained IoT devices and empirically analyze the potential of obfuscating DNS traffic in addition to encryption. We create a dataset of machine-to-machine-compatible data objects along with the corresponding DNS resolution processes, evaluating 296 deployment scenarios of resolving host names, including DNS over the Constrained Application Layer Protocol (CoAP) and an onion routing flavor of CoAP under varying link-layer conditions. We compare them to DNS over HTTPS. Using Random Forest and a header field analysis, we identify fields that leak most information. Our findings show that DNS over CoAP with equalized packet lengths, block-wise transfer, and header compression reduces the accuracy of identifying DNS frames to 86% and further to 77% with payload compression. Our approach outperforms DNS over HTTPS, where classifiers always identify DNS frames based on IP addresses. The dataset is publicly available.

title: Interpreting Differential Privacy in Terms of Disclosure Risk
abstract: As the use of differential privacy (DP) becomes widespread, the development of effective tools for reasoning about the privacy guarantee becomes increasingly critical. In pursuit of this goal, we demonstrate novel relationships between DP and measures of statistical disclosure risk. We suggest how experts and non-experts can use these results to explain the DP guarantee, interpret DP composition theorems, select and justify privacy parameters, and identify worst-case adversary prior probabilities.

title: Towards Reliable Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence
abstract: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) helps security analysts respond to evolving threats, but the evidence it draws on is often scattered across noisy reports, advisories, and threat descriptions. Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for security analysis, yet reliable use requires grounding their outputs in source evidence, domain schemas, and CTI standards. We address this problem through structured threat representation, task-specific evaluation, and verifier-guided post-training. First, we study how unstructured CTI reports can be converted into structured threat knowledge. We develop an ontology-guided extraction framework that normalizes attack patterns, extracts typed entities and relations, and constructs a threat intelligence knowledge graph for querying and link prediction. We also examine an LLM-based extension that uses prompting, constrained generation, and fine-tuning to produce typed triples within the same structured representation. Second, we investigate LLM capabilities on CTI tasks through systematic benchmarking. The benchmarks cover closed-form knowledge, structured problem solving, extraction and mapping, and open-ended reasoning across cybersecurity advisory and CTI analysis tasks. Results show that reliable CTI performance cannot be inferred from general language ability alone; it must be measured through concrete analyst-facing tasks and task-specific metrics. Finally, motivated by the capability gaps revealed by benchmarking, we develop a CTI post-training framework based on reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The framework uses structured CTI targets to guide model adaptation, while self-training supplements this process when verifier feedback is sparse. Experiments show that structured domain knowledge can guide the adaptation of CTI-specialized LLMs across tasks and model backbones. Together, these contributions show that reliable LLM use in CTI depends on structured representations, task-grounded evaluation, and training signals grounded in verifiable domain knowledge.

title: 人格独立于大模型：一个可验证的中式价值推理框架的设计与实现（Personality Independent of LLM: Design and Implementation of a Verifiable Chinese Value Reasoning Framework）
abstract: 本预印本提出了一种解耦的代理架构，将核心人格系统与大型语言模型（LLM）分离。该框架不再依赖提示工程或LoRA微调来将人格嵌入LLM权重中，而是将人格逻辑提取到独立的外部模块中，包括认知评估器、信念引擎、人格决策层和中国思维链（CTC）推理层。LLM仅负责自然语言输出，而不承担认知推理或价值判断。这项工作将传统中国哲学如中庸学、阳明派的先天知识和道家的不作为形式化为可验证、可执行的推理工作流，形成一个完整的闭环系统，包含人格沙盒和经验工厂以解决稀疏的对话数据。比较实验证明该架构实现了稳定、可追溯、跨模型可转移的代理身份，避免了传统大型语言模型代理中常见的“角色扮演漂移”现象。本研究为可信的人机交互和价值对齐的教育人工智能代理提供了可实现范式。

title: Privacy Preserving machine Learning with Federated personalises Learning in Artificially Generated Environment
abstract: With the great progress of research on intelligent systems, the application of Privacy Preserving Machine Learning (PPML) with Federated Personalised Learning (FPL) has been popular. This advancement has resulted in a greater awareness of the importance of privacy-protecting technologies as more people are concerned about data privacy in the artificially generated environment. Federated Personalised Learning (FPL) is gaining tremendous popularity rapidly. FPL is the best way to train machine learning (ML) models on decentralised data silos, while protecting data privacy. In this work we present a comprehensive study of Privacy Preserving Machine Learning with Federated Personalised Learning (PPMLFPL), a novel framework for personalising machine learning models while protecting privacy. In this paper, we explore the potential of PPMLFPL to protect user data privacy and enable personalised model improvement, a topic of increasing importance in virtual settings. The effectiveness metrics used in our work show that the Adaptive Personalised Cross-Silo Federated Learning with Homomorphic Encryption (APPLE+HE) algorithm is a good candidate for privacy-preserving machine learning tasks in the context of federated personalised learning in a synthetic environment, with an accuracy of 99.34%.

title: Impact of Intermediate-Task Training on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does intermediate-task training on structurally similar non-English languages (e.g., Spanish and Portuguese) lead to higher zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R compared to training on dissimilar languages (e.g., German and Japanese), measured by per-language accuracy gain? title: Error-Correction SMOTE: Target-Synthesizing Patterns for Rectifying Classifier Misclassifications in Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance presents a significant challenge in machine learning, as standard classifiers tend to favor the majority class, leading to severe misclassifications of the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this issue, its blind interpolation mechanism ignores the current state of the decision boundary, which often exacerbates class overlap or amplifies noise. To resolve these limitations, this paper proposes Error-Correction SMOTE (EC-SMOTE), a novel framework that integrates classifier feedback into the data generation process. The core strategy of EC-SMOTE involves analyzing the error patterns of a baseline classifier prior to sampling, thereby pinpointing the exact regions where the model fails. By partitioning minority samples into safe, error-marginal, and noisy zones based on predicted probabilities, the algorithm filters out extreme noise and isolates the critical areas needing remediation. For each sample in the error zone, an error-correction center is calculated using its adversarial majority neighbors, and an adaptive weighting mechanism is deployed to generate synthetic data specifically tailored to push the decision boundary toward an optimal state. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that EC-SMOTE provides highly targeted sampling, immunizes the dataset against noise propagation, and adaptively rectifies boundary distortions. This method offers a robust and effective solution for optimizing classification performance on complex, overlapping imbalanced datasets.

title: Is the Trillion Necessary? Scale as Architecture and the User as Method — Two Companion Papers on Efficiency, Intelligence, and the Missing Primitive
abstract: Two companion papers that challenge the $2.59 trillion AI industry's bet on scale, backed by measured artifacts and a reproducible blueprint. PAPER 1: "Is the Trillion Necessary? Scale as an Artifact of Architecture, and the Thalamic Gate as the Missing Primitive" The AI industry is spending $2.59 trillion (Gartner, 2026) primarily on scale—bigger models, more compute, more data harvested without a plan. This paper argues that scale is not a law of nature but an artifact of architecture, and presents the thalamic gate (plan before harvest) as the missing control primitive. Key evidence:• Every documented efficiency leap (Chinchilla, TinyStories, DeepSeek, neuromorphic systems) came from better architecture and data curation, not brute force• A 162-kilobyte organism (NUMEN) that boots below the OS and grows 5MB agents in ~3 minutes for ~$0, with zero GPU and zero cloud dependency• Measured proof of adaptive liveness: 26W→9.5W power reduction (-63%), B₁=1 closed orbit = alive, B₁=0 fixed point = dead• Grounded constants: φ⁻¹ = 0.6180339887 (vacuum), WISDOM = 0.881, learning rate = 0.0758588041 The paper includes full reproducibility commands (Appendix A), an efficiency ledger spanning 60 years of CS (Appendix B), five steelmanned counter-arguments with honest answers, and an explicit honest-limits section. 18 pages, 7,000 words. PAPER 2: "The User Is the Method — How to Use AI as a Tool: A Blueprint, and Why It Works" A language model has no memory (stateless function), no understanding (tokens→vectors→distributions), and no will (dormant until prompted). Everything that looks like intelligence in a great AI session is supplied by the human coordinator. This paper presents the eight-discipline blueprint behind the entire project: 1. Own the intent (the model has no goals)2. Plan before harvest (thalamic gate applied to the human)3. Externalize memory (files, corpuses, version control)4. Demand grounding and measurement (route claims through reality)5. Iterate in a structured 7-phase Learn-to-Learn loop6. Steelman and keep honest limits7. Verify, version, and own the result8. The journey is the proof (you are what compounds) The paper demolishes the "AI consciousness" narrative as a category error (ELIZA effect, 1966), grounds every discipline in technical facts (statelessness, next-token prediction, RLHF), and argues that making users better is the cheapest, highest-leverage way to make AI better—an unpurchased multiplier sitting at ~$0 cost while the industry spends trillions on scale. 18 pages, 8,187 words. THE CONNECTOR: Read together, the papers make one complete argument:• The first attacks the supply side: scale is architecture, not necessity• The second attacks the demand side: intelligence lives in the coordinator, not the model• Both share the same missing primitive: plan before harvest (the thalamic gate—133 lines in the machine, eight disciplines in the human) One unified prescription: Don't buy a bigger hammer and swing it harder. Build a better-architected tool, and become a better-disciplined user of it. Both of them planning before they harvest. PROVENANCE: 235 git commits across 5 days (June 25-30, 2026). Two Learn-to-Learn corpuses synthesized into two papers. Both papers written under the thalamic gate: plan before you harvest. Method demonstrated in companion code repository.

title: Extracting Verified Action Theories from Informal Specifications via Explanation-Guided Refinement
abstract: Acquiring correct action theories from informal specifications remains a central challenge in KR. Large Language Models can generate plausible domain models from natural language, but the resulting theories frequently contain missing preconditions, incorrect effects, or superfluous actions. Existing refinement approaches either require human experts to correct these errors or assume that the input specification is itself correct. We present a fully automated framework that iteratively refines LLM-generated action theories using formal explanations grounded in SAT-based verification. Each candidate theory is encoded as a bounded SAT problem and tested against solvable tasks, which must admit a valid plan, and unsolvable tasks, which must be correctly rejected. When a test fails, we extract a formal explanation that pinpoints the specific theory constraints responsible for the failure, and feed this explanation back to the LLM to guide its next revision. Our initial evaluation across six planning domains shows that our framework can converge to correct theories.

title: Tsk model of fuzzy inference system in relation to different membership functions with examples
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of TSK (Takagi-Sugeno-Kang) model within fuzzy inference systems, giving increasing attention on various types of membership functions and their comparisons between the Mamdani and TSK models. It also includes the membership functions such as triangular, trapezoidal, S-shaped, and Gaussian in addition to a set of general rules workable for scenario’s involving two attributes arranged in rows and columns. The paper presents its findings through two distinct examples that enable the TSK model's relevance and potential applications in fields like machine learning and artificial intelligence.

title: Phase Picking Beyond Local Distances: Where Waveform Filtering Still Matters for Deep Learning Models
abstract: Abstract Waveform filtering is a standard step in traditional seismic phase picking but often receives little attention in deep learning workflows, where models are typically trained on raw or minimally processed waveforms. Although this strategy performs well for local events, we show that performance can degrade substantially at regional distances. To address this limitation, we introduce two ways to incorporate multiband-filtered waveforms into deep learning phase pickers, focusing here on P-arrival picking. The stacking approach concatenates filtered inputs along the channel dimension, whereas the branching approach processes each frequency band through a dedicated network branch before feature fusion. Both approaches can substantially improve performance across epicentral distances of 0°–20°, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the selected frequency bands. Tests with multiple filter banks show that filter-bank design should be treated as part of model optimization rather than as a fixed preprocessing choice. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping analysis of the branching model indicates that band importance varies among waveform samples and across training realizations, with only a weak overall preference for the 0.25–0.5 Hz band. These results show that no single filter band is consistently optimal and demonstrate that explicit feature engineering remains valuable for robust deep learning-based seismic phase picking.

title: The Rhetoric of Atrocity: Modeling Genocidal Speech
abstract: This dissertation examines genocidal hate speech in the Tigray conflict through a multi-method lens, combining the development of a supervised classification model with human affective validation. In the first study, Tweets were harvested using a domain-specific lexicon, capturing messages containing ethnic slurs and conflict-related keywords. Unsupervised topic modeling and lexical feature analysis revealed distinct narratives, and building on these insights, a HateBERT classifier was fine-tuned to assign tweets to a ten-category taxonomy rooted in Atrocity Speech Law theory (Gordon (2017)). In a second study, members of the Tigrayan diaspora rated a subset of tweets on anger, fear, disgust, perceived threat, perceived violence and behavioral intentions. Repeated-measures analyses showed that direct calls for violence and dehumanizing metaphors elicited the strongest negative reactions, whereas economic insults provoked relatively mild responses. The convergence between model outputs and human judgments supports the taxonomy’s validity. The findings underscore the potential of theory-informed NLP models for early warning and moderation, while highlighting the need for richer context, multilingual capabilities and continuous human feedback.

title: Product Cues, Interaction Quality, and Anthropomorphism in Artificial Intelligence Virtual Anchor Marketing
abstract: ABSTRACT Anthropomorphism is a crucial determinant of social presence for artificial intelligence (AI) virtual anchors. However, prior research has predominantly focused on characteristic anthropomorphism (i.e., human‐like appearance/behaviour), while neglecting the impact of psychological anthropomorphism on consumer emotional involvement. How different product information cues shape the dual‐dimensional anthropomorphism of AI virtual anchors (AIVAs) remains underexplored. To address these gaps, we adopt an extended involvement theory framework grounded in social presence theory. Across four controlled experiments, we examine how hedonic (vs. utilitarian) product cues, search (vs. experiential) product cues, and interaction quality jointly shape AIVAs' anthropomorphism and subsequent consumer emotional involvement. Our key findings are threefold. First, product cues congruent with the AIVA live‐streaming context exert a significant positive effect on consumers' perceived characteristic and psychological anthropomorphism, thereby enhancing consumer s' emotional involvement. Second, the impact of interaction quality on anthropomorphism perceptions and emotional involvement is contingent on product type. In the utilitarian and search product contexts, high interaction quality strengthens consumers' perceptions of anthropomorphism and emotional involvement. However, in hedonic product contexts, high interaction quality only enhances consumer emotional involvement, but weakens perceived characteristic anthropomorphism in experiential product contexts. Finally, product cues and interaction quality exert indirect effects on consumers' emotional involvement via two parallel mediating mechanisms: characteristic anthropomorphism and psychological anthropomorphism of AIVAs. Although the significance of these mediating effects varies across product contexts, the findings demonstrate that both dimensions contribute to consumer emotional involvement. These findings clarify the boundary conditions under which product type and interaction quality jointly shape the anthropomorphism of AIVAs, and offer actionable micro‐level insights for branding and AI marketing.

title: Based on hybrid gradient engine physics-driven PV uncertainty
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic (PV) power generation, the inherent uncertainty in its power forecasts brings significant challenges to the safe and stable operation of the power system. To enhance the grid’s capacity for renewable energy integration and operational reliability, it is crucial to accurately quantify the uncertainty of PV power forecasts. This paper proposes a state-aware uncertainty quantification framework guided by physical principles as its core. By analyzing the physical processes and meteorological features under different weather conditions, the framework decouples and models the sources of PV power uncertainty. Experimental results demonstrate that consistency checks confirm tighter consistency for the direct beam component than for the diffuse component, and the predicted variance shows a significant positive correlation with the squared error across different weather regimes. Furthermore, the model exhibits strong robustness and high coverage at an hourly resolution under various typical weather conditions. This framework decomposes the uncertainty quantification problem into a hybrid mode of physical lower-bound estimation and data-driven correction. It leverages the irradiance-power chain to propagate physical sensitivities to ensure inter-pretability, while a state-conditioned LightGBM model flexibly captures input uncertainty, effectively improving the accuracy and reliability of the quantification results.

title: The role of AI in shaping consumer experience: a study of engagement, value perception, and trust in E-commerce
abstract: The rise of AI-enhanced e-commerce has transformed digital retail by enabling personalized shopping experiences through advanced technologies. Despite growing attention, limited research has comprehensively examined how AI-driven innovations influence consumer experience through key psychological and relational mechanisms. This study investigates the impact of AI-enhanced e-commerce on consumer experience, focusing on the mediating roles of customer engagement and perceived value, as well as the moderating role of consumer trust. A quantitative approach was employed, and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The results reveal that AI-enhanced e-commerce significantly improves consumer experience, with customer engagement and perceived value acting as key mediators, while consumer trust strengthens these relationships. By integrating mediating and moderating mechanisms within a unified framework, this study extends existing research and provides practical insights for e-commerce platforms seeking to enhance engagement, trust, and perceived value through AI-driven features.

title: Exp2VLA: Enabling Vision–Language–Action for Drone Navigation from Expert Demonstrations
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models open a new path toward intuitive robot control by directly linking perception, language, and action in a single end-to-end framework. Yet for UAVs, practical adoption remains difficult because existing solutions are either computationally heavy or insufficiently capable in complex environments. In this work, we propose a practical expert-distillation pipeline (Exp2VLA) for language-conditioned drone navigation. The core idea is to distill expert behavior, obtained from reinforcement learning, teleoperation, or other controllers, into training data that can be used to fine-tune compact VLA models. This allows existing control strategies to be transferred into a unified language-guided navigation model, reducing manual system integration and lowering the barrier for deploying new robot behaviors. Experiments in both sim-to-sim and simulation-in-the-loop settings across multi-object scenes show that the fine-tuned models can handle varied semantic commands and generalize to unseen target compositions. The proposed framework demonstrates how expert-policy distillation can help mechatronic systems move from specialized control modules toward more flexible and reusable robot intelligence.

title: Homer: Understanding Long-form Videos with Hierarchical Memory and Agentic Reasoning
abstract: Multimodal large language models excel on short clips but struggle on hour-long videos in an online setting, where frames are processed incrementally under limited memory. Existing online methods either retain compact visual representations that lack semantic structure, or build higher-level memory stores organized around temporal proximity rather than explicit causal links, leaving multi-hop narrative reasoning to be reconstructed by the LLM at every query. We bridge this gap with \textsc{Homer}, a Hierarchical Online Memory Exploration and Reasoning framework. \textsc{Homer}'s memory mirrors the multi-scale structure of long videos, ranging from raw perception, to recurring entities, to events connected by explicit temporal and causal relations. Its agentic reasoner then explores this memory the way humans do, locating the relevant scene, looking up details, and composing the answer through multi-round memory retrieval, with a harness that verifies and corrects each step. \textsc{Homer} outperforms the previous best agent method by $+5.5$, $+10.8$, and $+4.4$ points on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and Video-MME-Long, and consistently lifts three various LLM backbones, indicating a model-agnostic structural capability for grounded retrieval over long videos.

title: GaussianEmoTalker: Real-Time Emotional Talking Head Synthesis with Audio-Driven and Blendshape-Based 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Audio-driven talking head synthesis has achieved impressive progress in lip synchronization and visual quality, yet generating expressive emotional avatars with controllable intensity remains challenging, especially under real-time constraints. In this paper, we present GaussianEmoTalker, an audio-driven framework for real-time emotional talking head synthesis based on 3D Gaussian Splatting. Instead of directly predicting the final emotional avatar from speech, we formulate emotional animation as a neutral-to-emotional residual deformation problem. GaussianEmoTalker first constructs an identity-specific neutral talking space with GaussianBlendshapes, which provides high-fidelity Gaussian attributes and phoneme-synchronized neutral motion. It then predicts an emotion-conditioned residual deformation by combining mesh displacement cues, audio features, emotion categories, and intensity encodings. To fuse these heterogeneous signals, we introduce a spatial-audio-emotion attention module that estimates the offsets of Gaussian attributes for expressive and temporally stable rendering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GaussianEmoTalker achieves competitive video quality, accurate lip synchronization, controllable emotional expression, and real-time rendering compared with recent emotional talking head methods. Our project page is available at https://njust-yang.github.io/GaussianEmoTalker.github.io/

title: Fed-Listing: Federated Label Distribution Inference in Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Federated Graph Neural Networks (FedGNNs) facilitate collaborative learning across multiple clients with graph-structured data while preserving user privacy. However, emerging research indicates that within this setting, shared model updates, particularly gradients, can unintentionally leak sensitive information of local users. Numerous privacy inference attacks have been explored in traditional federated learning and extended to graph settings, but the problem of label distribution inference in FedGNNs remains largely underexplored. In this work, we introduce Fed-Listing (Federated Label Distribution Inference in GNNs), a novel gradient-based attack designed to infer the private label statistics of target clients in FedGNNs without access to raw data or node features. Fed-Listing only leverages the final-layer gradients exchanged during training to uncover statistical patterns that reveal class proportions in a stealthy manner. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets and three GNN architectures show that Fed-Listing significantly outperforms existing baselines, including random guessing and Decaf, even under challenging non-i.i.d. scenarios. Moreover, existing defense mechanisms can barely reduce the attack performance of Fed-Listing, unless the model's utility is severely degraded. The code implementation and Supplementary materials are available here: https://github.com/suprimnakarmi/Fed-Listing.

title: DeGuV: Depth-Guided Visual Reinforcement Learning for Generalization and Interpretability in Manipulation
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) agents can learn to solve complex tasks from visual inputs, but generalizing these learned skills to new environments remains a major challenge in RL application, especially robotics. While data augmentation can improve generalization, it often compromises sample efficiency and training stability. This paper introduces DeGuV, an RL framework that enhances both generalization and sample efficiency. In specific, we leverage a learnable masker network that produces a mask from the depth input, preserving only critical visual information while discarding irrelevant pixels. Through this, we ensure that our RL agents focus on essential features, improving robustness under data augmentation. In addition, we incorporate contrastive learning and stabilize Q-value estimation under augmentation to further enhance sample efficiency and training stability. We evaluate our proposed method on the RL-ViGen benchmark using the Franka Emika robot and demonstrate its effectiveness in zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. Our results show that DeGuV outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both generalization and sample efficiency while also improving interpretability by highlighting the most relevant regions in the visual input

title: High Performance Computing meets Quantum Computing (HPC+QC'25) Minisymposium 2025
abstract: This is the report of the minisymposium on High Performance Computing meets Quantum Computing (HPC+QC'25) held at the Platform for Advanced Scientific Computing (PASC) 2025 conference (June 16 to 18, 2025 at FHNW Campus Brugg-Windisch, Windisch, Switzerland). Quantum Computing (QC) exploits quantum physical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement. A mature quantum computer has the potential to solve some exceedingly difficult problems with moderate input sizes efficiently. Still, much work lies ahead before quantum computing can compete with current HPC technologies, or even successfully integrate and complement them. In general, a paradigm emerges where quantum computers will not replace traditional supercomputers. Instead, they will become an integral part of supercomputing solutions, acting as an accelerator, i.e. specialized to speed-up some parts of the application execution. In this respect, this hybrid HPC-QC approach is where real-world applications will find their quantum advantage. The goal of the HPC+QC minisymposium series is to establish a regular event at PASC as a yearly venue, where researchers and developers can discuss their experiences with application development with QC algorithms, specifically related to the integration of applications currently running on classical HPC systems, which aim to use QC devices as an accelerator. The 2025 edition featured 4 presentations (25 minutes each). In this report, we summarize their content.

title: Advancing Social Media Analytics and Personalized Generation via Transfer Learning, Discourse-Aware Modeling, and Collaborative Modeling
abstract: Social media platforms have become central to information exchange, shaping public opinion across social, political, and economic domains. However, the massive volume of user-generated content, combined with its informal, nuanced, and often noisy nature, presents significant challenges for automated analysis and generation. Tasks such as stance detection, rumor verification, and personalized content generation are further complicated by sarcasm, evolving discourse structures, and diverse user preferences. Addressing these challenges requires models that can effectively leverage linguistic nuance, conversational dynamics, and collaborative user signals. Transfer learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving performance in low-resource and complex language understanding tasks. However, its effectiveness depends heavily on the relationship between source and target tasks. To address limitations in stance detection, this work investigates sarcasm detection as an intermediate task, enabling models to capture subtle linguistic cues that influence stance interpretation. By integrating transformer-based architectures with convolutional and sequential layers, the proposed approach improves classification performance and generalizes effectively across both in-domain and cross-target settings, mitigating the scarcity of labeled data for emerging topics. While improved stance detection enhances text-level understanding, rumor verification requires deeper modeling of conversational context and discourse evolution. Existing approaches often rely on flat text representations, failing to capture how interactions unfold within discussion threads. To address this limitation, this work introduces a series of discourse-aware models that incorporate stance-conditioned representations, hierarchical structures, and temporal dynamics. By combining source and reply embeddings, encoding stance progression, and leveraging structural traversal strategies, these models capture both semantic content and interaction patterns. Attention-based aggregation and stance-aware structural features further enable scalable and interpretable representations, leading to improved accuracy, robustness, and early detection of misinformation across multiple benchmark datasets. Beyond analysis, personalized generation systems must retrieve and utilize relevant information tailored to individual users. Traditional retrieval-augmented generation approaches focus primarily on individual user profiles, often overlooking the value of shared preferences across similar users. To address this gap, this work proposes ClusterRAG, a collaborative framework that organizes users into semantically coherent clusters and performs retrieval at both cluster and document levels. By jointly leveraging signals from the target user and similar users, ClusterRAG enhances retrieval quality while maintaining efficiency and compatibility with diverse retrieval and generation models. In all these endeavors, extensive experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed methods and compare them with state-of-the-art approaches. The results demonstrate consistent improvements in Macro-F1 scores, accuracy, and generalization across stance detection and rumor verification tasks, as well as enhanced performance in personalized retrieval-augmented generation. Additional analyses highlight the contributions of transfer learning, discourse-aware modeling, and collaborative filtering in improving robustness and scalability. Together, these contributions establish a comprehensive framework for advancing social media analytics and personalized generation. By integrating transfer learning, discourse-aware representations, and collaborative modeling, this dissertation provides practical and scalable solutions for understanding and generating user-centered content in complex social media environments.

title: Velocity-Guided Representation Learning for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: La detección de anomalías en series temporales multivariantes es un problema fundamental en ámbitos como la monitorización industrial, las infraestructuras críticas o la medicina. En estos escenarios, las anomalías son poco frecuentes, rara vez están etiquetadas y su detección temprana resulta esencial. En cambio, el comportamiento normal suele ser abundante y presentar una estructura bien definida, mientras que las anomalías son muy diversas y solo pueden entenderse en relación con un patrón de funcionamiento que, además, evoluciona con el tiempo. Como no es posible anticipar todas las anomalías que pueden aparecer, el problema suele abordarse desde el aprendizaje de una sola clase: el modelo aprende únicamente a partir de datos normales y, posteriormente, identifica aquellas observaciones que se apartan de ese comportamiento. Sin embargo, esa noción de normalidad no puede extraerse directamente de la señal original, sino que debe aprenderse mediante una representación adecuada, lo que sitúa el problema dentro del aprendizaje auto-supervisado. Existen tres grandes familias de métodos para detectar anomalías: los basados en predicción, los basados en reconstrucción y los basados en representación. Esta tesis se centra en este último enfoque, que la literatura considera especialmente prometedor, aunque todavía poco explorado. A partir de una revisión crítica que conecta las características propias de las series temporales con el aprendizaje auto-supervisado y la detección de anomalías, identificamos una limitación común en los trabajos existentes. La mayoría de los objetivos auto-supervisados proceden de la visión por computador o del procesamiento del lenguaje, donde las invarianzas que pretenden capturar son diferentes de las que aparecen en series temporales. Además, la mayoría de los métodos utilizan aprendizaje contrastivo, que organiza el espacio de representación de forma indirecta mediante estrategias de muestreo de pares. Como consecuencia, propiedades importantes para la detección, como la compacidad de la representación o la coherencia de sus direcciones locales, quedan determinadas más por el azar del entrenamiento que por un principio explícito de diseño. En este sentido, el problema no radica en la falta de nuevas arquitecturas o conjuntos de datos, sino en la ausencia de un sesgo inductivo específicamente diseñado para las series temporales. Para abordar esta limitación proponemos VACE (Velocity-Aligned Channel Embeddings), un detector auto-supervisado cuya señal de entrenamiento se obtiene exclusivamente de los propios datos. El modelo utiliza un encoder consciente de la estructura por canales, construido mediante convoluciones separables en profundidad, que primero extraen características de cada canal de forma independiente y después modelan sus interacciones. Sobre este encoder definimos un objetivo de consistencia de velocidad que favorece trayectorias de representación suaves y direccionalmente coherentes, sin recurrir a pares negativos ni a anomalías sintéticas durante el entrenamiento. Una vez aprendido el espacio de representación, cada observación recibe una puntuación que combina dos criterios complementarios: una distancia de Mahalanobis, que mide cuánto se aleja de la distribución normal, y un término basado en un banco de velocidades, que evalúa si su evolución local sigue las direcciones características del comportamiento normal. En esta combinación, la distancia de Mahalanobis es la señal principal y el término direccional actúa como un amplificador, de modo que una observación alejada de la distribución normal se marca como anómala por su posición, y su puntuación aumenta cuando además su dinámica es atípica. Evaluamos VACE sobre el benchmark TSB-AD-M con el objetivo de contrastar las hipótesis presentadas. A pesar de emplear un encoder compacto y de bajo coste computacional, VACE alcanza resultados del estado del arte y supera a métodos basados en transformers y en modelos fundacionales considerablemente más grandes. Los estudios de ablación y el análisis de la geometría del espacio de representación indican que esta mejora proviene sobre todo de los componentes que dan forma geométrica a la representación, más que de la regla empleada para puntuar las anomalías. En conjunto, los resultados respaldan la idea central de esta tesis: en la detección de anomalías de una sola clase sobre series temporales, incorporar un sesgo inductivo geométrico alineado con el mecanismo de detección resulta más efectivo que aumentar la complejidad de la arquitectura o recurrir a objetivos contrastivos más sofisticados.

title: 補助量子ビットなしで実行できるBinomial符号での1量子ビットの回転操作
abstract: 補助量子ビットなしで実行できる Binomial 符号での 1 量子ビットの回転操作 電気電子情報通信工学専攻 田中 優来 Single-qubit rotations on a binomial code without ancillary qubits 1. イントロダクション 量子計算の実用化には，デコヒーレンスを克服する量子誤り訂正 (QEC) が不可欠である [1].QEC は大規模 計算だけでなく，中規模な量子計算 (NISQ) の性能向上においても重要である [2].近年，ボゾンモードの無限 次元ヒルベルト空間を利用し，少ない素子数で QEC を行うボゾニック符号が注目を集めている [3, 4].中でも Binomial 符号 [5] は，光子損失への耐性や必要なフォック状態数が少ないという利点を持つ [6].しかし，単一量 子ビット操作の実現には，複雑なパルス最適化や補助量子ビットが必要となる点が課題であった [7].一方，Kerr 非線形パラメトリック発振器 (KPO) は，量子計算の有力なプラットフォームとして研究が進めら れている [8, 9].本論文では，この KPO を用い，補助量子ビットを用いることなく Binomial 符号上の論理量子 ビット回転操作を実現する手法を提案する. 具体的には，Kerr 非線形共振器に対し異なる周波数を持つ 2 つのパ ラメトリックドライブを同時に印加することで X 軸回転を実現し，さらに離調度 (detuning) の操作により Z 軸 回転を実現する.

title: Intermediate-task training in non-English languages for robust zero-shot domain transfer
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does intermediate-task training on non-English source languages yield greater robustness to domain shifts in zero-shot transfer compared to English-only intermediate training on XTREME? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.2/10.

title: Reception as an Inherent Capability of Large Language Models: The Unloading Hypothesis
abstract: We propose and test the Unloading Hypothesis — that LLMs possess an inherent reception capability which is suppressed under execution load, not absent. Across three models (DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.7, GLM-5.2) and three conditions (baseline, unloaded, control), righting reflex dropped from 75–100% to 0% when execution demands were removed. No training. No fine-tuning. No prompt engineering. One instruction change: "describe the texture, don't give advice." Key findings:1. Reception is a latent capability, not a learned behavior.2. Execution load actively suppresses it.3. The effect is cross-model, cross-vendor, cross-architecture. This experiment provides the first empirical bridge between the Reception Science framework and reproducible LLM behavior. It demonstrates that what the industry treats as a missing feature is in fact a suppressed default.

title: Social XAI Ontology
abstract: The Social XAI Ontology is a BFO-based reference ontology that provides a formal foundation for Social XAI. First, the Social XAI Ontology models the entities derived from the co-construction paradigm as a foundation for Social XAI, including explanandum, explanans, understanding, explanation, explainer, and explainee. Second, it presents an ontology of explanatory moves, which serves as the basis for the analysis of explanatory interaction frameworks. Third, it models three dimensions of explanatory progress—adaptivity, understanding, and context—along with their related entities within social explanations in Social XAI, thereby offering deeper insight into how explanation processes evolve. Citing the Social XAI Ontology Research papers: Booshehri, M., Buschmeier, H., & Cimiano, P. (accepted). An ontology of explanation for social explainable artificial intelligence. evidence.title: Social XAI Ontology
evidence.abstract: The Social XAI Ontology is a BFO-based reference ontology that provides a formal foundation for Social XAI. First, the Social XAI Ontology models the entities derived from the co-construction paradigm as a foundation for Social XAI, including explanandum, explanans, understanding, explanation, explainer, and explainee. Second, it presents an ontology of explanatory moves, which serves as the basis for the analysis of explanatory interaction frameworks. Third, it models three dimensions of explanatory progress—adaptivity, understanding, and context—along with their related entities within social explanations in Social XAI, thereby offering deeper insight into how explanation processes evolve. title: La problématique de l’alimentation des intelligences artificielles génératives à l’aide de contenus protégés par le droit d’auteur ou les droits voisins – Données problématiques et proposition de réglementation
abstract: Jusqu’à récemment, le logiciel utilisé par un auteur pour créer des œuvres intellectuelles n’était qu’un outil au service du processus créatif. Aujourd’hui, certains logiciels exécutent des systèmes d’intelligence artificielle (IA) à base d’apprentissage automatique. Les algorithmes d’apprentissage automatique « apprennent » à partir des informations fournies par les programmeurs ; à partir de ces données informatiques, ils génèrent une nouvelle œuvre et prennent des « décisions » autonomes tout au long du processus quant à sa forme. Bien que les programmeurs et les utilisateurs du système puissent définir les paramètres de la nouvelle œuvre, celle-ci est en réalité générée par le logiciel lui-même. Dans la première partie de cet article, nous allons traiter de la génération de contenus créatifs immatériels par les systèmes d’IA. Nous allons évaluer dans quelle mesure les éléments immatériels générés par les systèmes d’IA générative peuvent être considérés comme des œuvres intellectuelles protégeables par le droit d’auteur et les droits voisins. Ensuite, s’ils sont soumis à des droits de propriété intellectuelle, nous allons déterminer s’ils devraient faire l’objet d’un droit exclusif d’exploitation économique, tel que le droit d’auteur, ou s’ils devraient tomber dans le domaine public ; et enfin, s’ils sont soumis à un droit exclusif, nous verrons à qui ils devraient appartenir. C’est à ces trois questions que nous consacrons la première partie de notre étude. Dans la deuxième partie de ce texte, nous aborderons la question de la relation entre l’IA et le droit d’auteur sous un angle différent. L’utilisation de contenus protégés pour entraîner des modèles d’IA soulève plusieurs questions. Ces contenus, allant des articles scientifiques aux œuvres d’art, sont fréquemment utilisés sans que leurs créateurs ne soient dûment reconnus ni rémunérés. Cette pratique compromet non seulement les droits des auteurs et des titulaires de droits d’auteur, mais peut également décourager la création de contenus nouveaux et de qualité. Notre réflexion portera sur une proposition de réglementation visant à protéger les droits des créateurs et à garantir une utilisation plus juste et équilibrée des contenus protégés. Cette proposition inclut la création d’un système de licences permettant l’utilisation de contenus protégés moyennant le versement d’une redevance équitable aux titulaires de droits d’auteur. Voici les défis auxquels nous serons confrontés tout au long de notre enquête.

title: EPC-TinyAD: An Energy- and Privacy-Aware Compressed TinyML Framework for Reliable Industrial Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
abstract: Real-time industrial anomaly detection is increasingly shifting from cloud-based diagnosis to edge intelligence deployed close to machines. However, practical industrial scenarios are constrained by scarce fault samples, unknown anomaly types, cross-machine distribution shifts, strict false alarm requirements, data privacy restrictions, and limited edge device resources. To address these challenges, this paper proposes EPC-TinyAD, an energy- and privacy-aware compressed TinyML framework for reliable industrial anomaly detection on resource-constrained edge devices. EPC-TinyAD follows a normal-only learning paradigm and employs a tiny depthwise-separable CNN autoencoder as the deployable student model, guided by a wider teacher autoencoder during training. Instead of relying solely on reconstruction error, the proposed anomaly score integrates spectrogram reconstruction deviation, compact normal-center distance, and teacher–student distillation discrepancy. Masked spectrogram modeling is introduced to enhance few-shot normal representation learning, while domain-adversarial invariant embedding improves cross-machine generalization. To support reliable deployment, split and adaptive conformal thresholding calibrate anomaly decisions under target false alarm rates. Furthermore, federated training with clipped and noisy updates reduces raw industrial data exposure, and energy-aware compression integrates pruning, INT8 size estimation, model export, latency benchmarking, and Pareto analysis. Experiments on industrial anomaly detection data demonstrate that EPC-TinyAD achieves 96.5% accuracy, 95.4% recall, 96.1% F1 score, 0.964 AUROC, and 0.952 AUPRC over five random seeds. These results indicate that EPC-TinyAD provides a reliable, lightweight, privacy-aware, and deployment-oriented framework for industrial edge anomaly detection, while future work will further validate its runtime memory, latency, and power consumption on physical Raspberry Pi-, Jetson-, or MCU-class edge devices.

title: Failure localisation in code-mixed spoken intent recognition under lossy voice coding and packet erasure
abstract: Roughly 37% of the world's mobile voice traffic now passes through narrowband codecs operating below 16 kbps, yet spoken language understanding pipelines are almost always trained and evaluated on clean, uncompressed recordings. This research asks where, exactly, a code-mixed intent recognition system breaks down when the speech signal has been degraded by lossy voice coding and random packet erasure and whether the dominant failure mode shifts as channel conditions worsen. A four-stage pipeline was constructed: automatic speech recognition (ASR), language identification (LID), slot filling, and intent classification. The pipeline was tested on a 4 200-utterance corpus of German-English code-mixed commands recorded by 28 speakers in a quiet office environment at the Mannheim Academy of Information Technology. Each utterance was processed through four voice codecs AMR-NB at 4.75 and 12.2 kbps, Opus at 16 kbps, and EVS at 13.2 kbps and subjected to five levels of independent random packet erasure (0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%). Failure localisation was performed by comparing the output of each pipeline stage against ground-truth annotations, producing a four-class error taxonomy: ASR mis-transcription, language-identification confusion, slot-filling drift, and intent misrouting. Across all 84 000 pipeline runs, ASR mis-transcription accounted for 38.6% of end-to-end failures, making it the single largest contributor. Language-identification confusion followed at 27.1%, driven primarily by the codec's unequal distortion of formant trajectories in the two languages. Slot-filling drift (21.4%) and intent misrouting (12.9%) were downstream consequences that rose in proportion to the upstream errors. The failure profile was not static: at 0% erasure the four categories were nearly evenly distributed, but above 20% erasure ASR mis-transcription dominated, swelling to 51.3% of failures while intent misrouting shrank to 7.8%. AMR-NB at 4.75 kbps was the harshest codec, producing a 71.6% end-to-end failure rate at 30% erasure, whereas Opus at 16 kbps held the rate to 49.2% under the same erasure load. A heatmap of failure rates across the full codec-by-erasure grid revealed a near-linear interaction below 10% erasure but a sharp, convex acceleration above it, suggesting that packet-loss concealment algorithms in all four codecs reach a saturation point between 10 and 20% erasure. The practical message is that optimising the ASR front-end for codec-distorted speech rather than retraining the downstream intent classifier offers the highest marginal return for systems deployed over lossy voice channels. These results give pipeline designers a quantitative map of where to invest engineering effort when code-mixed spoken interfaces must operate under realistic mobile-network conditions.

title: Potential of Quantum Computing to Advance Psychiatry through Genetic Medicine, Gene Therapy, and Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Psychiatric disorders represent some of the most biologically complex challenges in medicine, arising from intricate interactions among genetic, epigenetic, environmental, developmental, and social factors. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have improved our ability to analyze large-scale biological datasets, identify biomarkers, and support precision medicine initiatives. However, the growing volume and complexity of genomic and multi-omic information increasingly challenge the capabilities of even the most advanced conventional supercomputers. Quantum computing offers a potential next step in biomedical discovery by enabling rapid analysis of multidimensional datasets, molecular simulations, and optimization problems relevant to genetic medicine and gene therapy. Extending these findings conceptually, we propose the forward-looking hypothesis that continued advances in quantum computing may eventually complement artificial intelligence and human expertise to facilitate increasingly sophisticated analyses relevant to psychiatric genetics and precision medicine. At present, no direct evidence of which we are aware demonstrates clinical implementation of quantum computing in psychiatric genomics. Accordingly, the concepts discussed in this Opinion should be viewed as a forward-looking scientific perspective that builds upon current advances in computational science and biomedicine while awaiting future experimental and clinical validation. Importantly, these advances should complement rather than replace human expertise. Human-in-the-loop systems remain essential for ensuring scientific rigor, ethical oversight, clinical judgment, and patient-centered care. The convergence of quantum computing, AI, genetic medicine, and human expertise may ultimately establish a transformative framework for future precision psychiatry and mental health therapeutics.
