title: MAPPING CONSISTENT STYLISTIC PATTERNS OF UNDERGRADUATE LEARNERS ACROSS WRITING TEXTS
abstract: This study investigates the consistency of writing style (or stylistic biometric identity) of undergraduate students engaged in different writing tasks. With the growing use of computer writing and computer-supported writing tools, author verification and support for academic integrity are increasingly important. Here, this study adopts a quantitative approach to computational stylometry. The samples were purposively selected 100 undergraduate students and constructed a corpus of students' work, including several writing samples for each essay, report, and reflective task. Stylometric features of interest included vocabulary, syntax, sentence length, word frequency, and readability index—descriptive statistics indicating low variability in the selected features and stylistic consistency among students. Set out to confirm these observations by means of inferential statistics. There were no significant differences in most writing tasks (p > 0.05) as reported by the paired-samples t-test, reaffirming stylistic consistency. However, there were differences (p < 0.05) between the high- and low-stylistically consistent groups, as assessed by an independent-samples t-test, for lexical diversity and syntactic complexity. Also found a high positive correlation between lexical diversity and stylistic consistency (r = 0.58); readability and consistency (r = 0.49), and a moderately negative correlation between syntactic complexity and consistency (r = -0.52), according to the correlation test. The accuracy of predicted stylistic consistency for all the students is 82%. Findings show that students typically maintain a consistent writing style across different writing tasks, with minor variations due to the writing context. Research demonstrates the use of stylometric analysis for individualized learning, author recognition, and academic plagiarism detection. Findings can be improved by training the system with more sophisticated natural language processing approaches and larger datasets to enhance generalization. Keywords: Stylometry, writing style, undergraduate learners, computational Linguistics, Academic integrity, ESL writing, text analysis.

title: Chamlon: disseny i implementació d’una VPN resistent a l’anàlisi de trànsit
abstract: La privacitat digital s'ha convertit en un dels reptes centrals de les xarxes de comunicacions actuals. Tot i que el contingut del trànsit es protegeix habitualment mitjançant xifratge, un observador situat en un punt intermedi de la xarxa (un proveïdor d'accés, un operador de xarxa mòbil o un tercer amb capacitat de vigilància) pot seguir obtenint informació rellevant sense necessitat de desxifrar res: la metadada de la comunicació. Aquesta metadada inclou, entre altres coses, la mida dels paquets, la seva cadència temporal, els pics i valls de l'activitat, i els patrons de trànsit resultants. A partir d'aquesta informació és possible inferir el tipus d'aplicació utilitzada, distingir trànsit de veu, vídeo o navegació web, o fins i tot correlacionar sessions amb activitats concretes mitjançant tècniques d'anàlisi de trànsit (traffic analysis). Aquest problema es coneix com a metadata leakage, i és independent de la fortalesa del xifratge emprat.Aquest projecte implementa una VPN orientada a la protecció no només del contingut sinó també dels patrons de trànsit. El projecte es complementa amb una interfície gràfica d'usuari (GUI) desenvolupada en PyQt5, que permet configurar i monitoritzar la connexió sense necessitat d'interactuar directament amb la línia de comandes, facilitant així l'ús de l'eina per part d'un usuari final.

title: Quantifying emergent logic to detect hallucinations in transformer architectures
abstract: En aquest treball es presenta l'estudi que s'ha fet en relació amb el càlcul d'emergència en els LLMs. L'Emergència és una propietat relacionada amb la teoria de la informació que poden presentar certs sistemes. Segons el reduccionisme, un sistema pot ser entès de la millor manera quan el mirem a l'escala més petita, a nivell dels àtoms més petits que el conformen. No obstant, certs sistemes presenten més informació causal en algunes agregacions superiors a la de nivell micro. És a dir, agregant certs estats del sistema, podem tenir més clares les causes dels efectes i els efectes de les causes. L'explicabilitat dels LLMs és un problema que es presenta en el món de la ciència de dades. Ara mateix hi ha una gran varietat de camps d'investigació que hi estan fent avanços, amb diferents perspectives o filosofies i mètodes d'acció. No obstant, el càlcul de l'emergència en els LLMs no és un camp que sigui reconegut ni visible de moment. En el que treballa aquesta tesis és en demostrar que en certs entorns i sota certes condicions, els LLMs poden presentar emergència, i que per tant, l'explicabilitat pot no residir en l'estudi de cada una de les neurones del model per separat. L'estudi presenta un experiment en el que es demostra l'aparició d'emergència en un sistema en l'espai d'estats d'un LLM amb certes restriccions. L'experiment utilitza el dataset 'Indirect Object Identification' per produir una sèrie de prompts en els que es demana que el LLM trobi l'objecte indirecte d'una sentència i l'escrigui en el següent token. Mitjançant la múltiple realització de l'experiment amb una gran quantitat de frases que compleixen aquest criteri, s'estima una Matriu de Transició de Probabilitats del sistema. Una vegada definit el sistema, es calcula l'emergència del mateix utilitzant les definicions proposades per Erik Hoel, l'autor del primer paper sobre aquest camp.

title: Quantum Dot Spin Dynamics and Quantum Randomness for Secure Optical Communication
abstract: This thesis investigates two complementary quantum technologies for secure optical communication: spin dynamics in telecom C-band quantum dots and a high-bandwidth source-device-independent quantum random number generator. Together, they address two central requirements of quantum networks: long-lived spin memories for quantum repeaters and secure, high-rate entropy generation for quantum key distribution. The first part studies the spin dynamics of InAs/InGaAs/InP quantum dots grown by strain-free droplet epitaxy using time-resolved Faraday ellipticity. Compared to Stranski-Krastanov grown telecom dots, droplet epitaxy shows improved spin properties, including an electron spin relaxation time of 3.0 us and reduced in-plane electron g-factor anisotropy, indicating enhanced structural symmetry. Polarization recovery and Hanle measurements reveal nuclear spin lifetimes comparable to electron spin lifetimes, attributed to quadrupolar interactions arising from Ga-In interdiffusion. These results demonstrate the advantages of droplet epitaxy over strain-based growth and indicate further potential through optimized material compositions. The second part investigates one-, two-, and four-layer InAs/InAlGaAs Stranski-Krastanov quantum dots to assess layer-dependent carrier type and spin coherence. Increasing layer number induces a transition from electron to hole resident carriers due to interlayer tunnelling into lower-energy dots, the emergence of spin-mode locking for four or more layers, and the appearance of a non-oscillating spin component likely associated with reduced heavy-hole/light-hole mixing. Although droplet epitaxy samples exhibit superior spin parameters overall, no spin-mode locking is observed, potentially due to shorter transverse coherence or electron-dominated charging. The final part presents a source-device-independent quantum random number generator based on heterodyne detection of vacuum fluctuations. Using a 90 degree optical hybrid, balanced photodetectors, a dual-channel 12-bit ADC operating at 3.2 GS/s per channel, and FPGA-implemented Toeplitz hashing with PCIe transfer, a total extracted bandwidth of 33.91 Gbit/s is achieved. The system assumes no trust in the optical source and performs all extraction in hardware, maintaining security even under adversarial state preparation.

title: BU217 Refined p^w Audit Grammar and Symbolic Interface under B_U BU217 B_U 体系下精炼 p^w 审计语法与符号接口
abstract: Abstract BU217, p^w Symbolic Interface and Cross-Domain Audit Grammar under B_U, consolidates the preceding regime-switching files into a unified symbolic interface for auditing transitions across public policy, social governance, AI alignment, behavioral intervention, organizational transformation, platform governance, and multi-agent systems. Its central claim is that p^w should not remain an intuitive phrase such as “weak persistence,” “repairability,” or “controlled transition.” Under the B_U framework, p^w functions as a formal audit interface: a way to determine whether a transition path can preserve SourceAxis continuity, pay its friction cost, stratify its residual burden, retain rollback and repair capacity, and produce positive standing after real-world settlement. The file defines the core symbolic grammar of p^w audit. A regime-switching path is represented as π: R_old → R_transition → R_new, where each regime has its own carrier structure, cost surface, residual field, and feedback loop. SourceAxis, denoted as S_A, identifies the grounding condition that must remain continuous throughout the transition. Carrier mapping identifies the real substrates through which the transition must be carried: institutions, organizations, humans, AI models, platforms, markets, legal systems, tools, feedback channels, or multi-agent networks. C_fric represents the total friction cost of transition: fiscal, behavioral, administrative, cognitive, verification, trust, coordination, governance, legacy, rollback, and repair costs. Xi_res represents the residual field left by the transition: unresolved costs, trust decay, behavioral debt, misalignment residue, coordination failure, legitimacy loss, tool-use escalation, or intergenerational burden. Standing represents the final admissibility verdict after gain, cost, residuals, and repair capacity have been counted. BU217’s main contribution is to make p^w portable without making it vague. Across earlier files, p^w appears in different domains: social governance switching, public-policy audit, behavioral friction, behavioral bias, nudge theory, dual-process nudging, residual metrics, AI alignment, AI-alignment audit, C_fric metrics, and multi-agent mechanism design. BU217 shows that these domains share a common audit structure. They differ in carriers, residual types, and domain-specific friction, but they all require the same settlement logic: no transition is admissible merely because its target state looks superior. The path must remain weakly persistent while moving through reality. The file also distinguishes p^w from perfect stability, full optimization, and static correctness. Weak persistence does not require the absence of error, uncertainty, local deviation, implementation unevenness, or temporary instability. It requires that deviation remains bounded, SourceAxis remains continuous, residuals remain visible, rollback remains possible, repair paths remain active, feedback remains informative, and standing does not collapse. This makes p^w the correct interface for real transitions, where complete certainty is impossible and rigid perfection often creates more fragility than resilience. BU217 therefore serves as the symbolic closure file for the current audit sequence. It gives the B_U framework a reusable regime-switching grammar: define π, lock S_A, map carriers, compute C_fric, stratify Xi_res, verify p^w repairability, evaluate standing, and issue a verdict. Under B_U, a system becomes transition-admissible only when it can pass this full symbolic chain. p^w is the formal name for a transition that can move, absorb, repair, and still stand.

title: Multilingual Intermediate-Task Training and Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance on XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does multilingual intermediate-task training affect zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance compared to monolingual English training on XTREME-R when evaluated using the XTREME-R benchmark score? title: Research on Causal SMOTE Oversampling Algorithm Based on Causally Interpretable Feature Paths
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often leading classifiers to bias toward the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to address this issue by interpolating between minority examples, it relies strictly on statistical correlations and Euclidean distances within the feature space. Consequently, traditional SMOTE frequently interpolates along paths of spurious correlation, generating logically invalid "ghost samples" that distort decision boundaries and degrade model generalization. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel oversampling algorithm named Causal SMOTE. The core philosophy of this method is to restrict and guide sample generation strictly through a causal lens. By utilizing structural causal models (SCM) to learn the underlying directed acyclic graph (DAG) of the data, the algorithm screens out spurious associations and extracts "causally interpretable feature paths" directly linked to the target variable. Furthermore, an oversampling constraint mechanism is designed based on the Average Causal Effect (ACE), assigning weights to feature dimensions to adjust their interpolation ranges while freezing non-causal dimensions. By preventing sample generation along misleading paths, Causal SMOTE preserves the authentic causal mechanisms of the minority class and mitigates confounding biases. This research provides a new, causally explainable perspective for handling imbalanced datasets and significantly enhances the robustness and interpretability of classification boundaries.

Furthermore, an oversampling constraint mechanism is designed based on the Average Causal Effect (ACE), assigning weights to feature dimensions to adjust their interpolation ranges while freezing non-causal dimensions. By preventing sample generation along misleading paths, Causal SMOTE preserves the authentic causal mechanisms of the minority class and mitigates confounding biases. This research provides a new, causally explainable perspective for handling imbalanced datasets and significantly enhances the robustness and interpretability of classification boundaries.

title: OptimSolution: A Cross-Platform Framework for Benchmarking, Sensitivity, and Complexity Analysis of Continuous Optimisation Methods
abstract: We present OptimSolution, an open-source, cross-platform framework for the systematic benchmarking and analysis of continuous optimisation methods, available for Windows, Linux and macOS and operable via both a command-line interface (CLI) and a Qt-based Graphical User Interface (GUI). The framework supports four execution modes: Single mode for single method–problem runs with convergence and distribution analysis; Batch mode for automated multi-method, multi-problem experimentation with aggregated statistical summaries; Method Sensitivity Analysis for quantifying the effect of algorithmic hyperparameters on solution quality; and Problem Sensitivity Analysis for assessing how problem-defining parameters influence instance difficulty and inter-method rankings. Complexity analysis is provided along two-axes method scalability across problem dimensionalities and problem difficulty profiles across method portfolios. Statistical validation is embedded natively through Wilcoxon signed-rank and Friedman tests with post-hoc pairwise analysis, complemented by rank tables and box-plot visualisations. All outputs are exportable as CSV files or publication-ready PNG figures. The framework is designed for extensibility: new methods and benchmark problems can be registered and activated through the GUI without modifications to the core codebase, supporting rapid experimental iteration.

title: Handing over control: A longitudinal study of delegation and disclosure in human-AI interaction
abstract: The increasing integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into everyday tasks raises important questions about how individuals rely on these systems in the long run. While prior research has primarily examined cross-sectional predictors of AI use, little is known about how willingness to delegate tasks and disclose information to AI develops over time. The present study addresses this gap examining a six-wave longitudinal survey (N = 1,008 at baseline) conducted over ten months with a U.S. sample. We investigated changes in willingness to delegate professional and personal writing tasks to AI, as well as willingness to disclose information to AI, and tested the influence of user-related (experience, frequency of use, attitudes, and knowledge) and AI-related evaluative factors (trust, anthropomorphism, social actor perception). Contrary to expectations, willingness to delegate and disclose decreased over time, with the decline attenuating across waves. Willingness to delegate remained consistently higher for professional than for personal tasks. Use frequency, positive attitudes, trust, and anthropomorphism were associated with greater willingness to delegate, whereas experience and social actor perception showed no consistent effects. Willingness to disclose was similarly shaped by use and attitudinal factors. These findings suggest that human-AI interaction reflects a process of calibration rather than increasing reliance, highlighting the importance of temporal dynamics in understanding AI adoption and use.

title: Educational robots for student creativity development: Research trends and evidence from topic modeling, meta-analysis, and rule mining
authors: Xieling Chen, Haoran Xie, Xiaohui Tao, Lin Li, Xingquan Peng and Fu Lee Wang
abstract: With the increasing adoption of educational robots (ERs) to support creativity development, a comprehensive understanding of their research landscape, empirical effectiveness, and instructional conditions becomes necessary. This study addresses this need by proposing a three-stage analytical framework that involves topic modeling, meta-analysis, and rule mining. First, a BERTopic modeling approach was applied to identify four major research topics, including STEAM motivation and gamified project-based learning, creative coding and narrative play in early childhood, pedagogies for creative and computational thinking, and creative engineering and physical computing, with a growing emphasis on narrative and constructionist approaches, especially in early childhood education. Second, a Bayesian meta-analysis was utilized to identify a moderate overall effect size (Mean = 0.600), with subgroup analyses demonstrating that effect sizes varied significantly across experimental design factors such as subject domain, age group, learning duration, setting, instructional strategy, and measurement issue, where studies focusing on programming education, preschool and high school learners, and guided learning yielded the strongest effects. Finally, an associate rule mining approach was used to identify consistent patterns linking skill modeling, robot-as-tool roles, and mixed instructional strategies with positive creativity outcomes. Findings of this study contribute to both research and practice by enhancing researchers’ and instructors’ understanding of ER research trends and practical effectiveness in promoting creativity, with actionable instructional design recommendations being provided to optimize ER-based creativity interventions.

title: A Normal Form for Rules Containing Arithmetic Operations
abstract: This paper describes the process of translating rules that may contain arithmetic operations into the language of first-order logic. It identifies a normal form for which this transformation can be performed in a particularly simple and natural way. Other rules can be converted to this normal form by steps that preserve their meaning under the stable model semantics.

title: Statistical analysis of bigram patterns in domain-specific texts for improved classification accuracy
abstract: Specialized text classification systems have two problems: poor contextualization with just unigrams, and high class imbalance that skews the statistical models toward the majority classes. In this paper, we present a hybrid approach that combines the statistical bigram approach with the deep generative approach of text generation to overcome these obstacles. The feature extraction was done through three weighting schemes: Term Presence, Term Frequency, and Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). Academic and financial data were imbalanced, with 70% data for the academic and 15% data for the financial. Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest and AdaBoost were used on the imbalanced data sets. Minority class scarcity was overcome by creating synthetic texts with LSTM and fine-tuned GPT-2, and the semantic quality was ensured by the cosine similarity threshold set at ≥ 0.75. The analysis of results showed that the TF-IDF weighting using bigrams performed the best. The Macro F1-score was improved by more than 20% in both domains, with the performance of minority classes almost doubled after the text generation. These improvements were indeed statistically significant (p < 0.01) with large practical effect size, as confirmed by statistical tests (paired t-test and Cohen's d). The suggested framework provides a viable approach that can be replicated to improve the accuracy of the text classification in a specific domain with limited amounts and imbalanced data.

title: A Federated Learning Framework for Predictive Maintenance in IoT-Enabled Smart Environments
abstract: Predictive maintenance is a critical component in the management of smart environments, aiming to reduce unplanned downtimes and enhance operational efficiency. Conventional centralized machine learning approaches often pose challenges regarding data privacy, latency, and scalability, particularly in IoT-enabled systems with distributed sensor networks. In response to these limitations, this paper proposes a novel federated learning framework designed for predictive maintenance tasks in smart environments. The framework allows decentralized model training directly on edge devices without transmitting raw data, thereby preserving user privacy and minimizing communication overhead. The system integrates an LSTM-based autoencoder for time-series anomaly detection, tailored for resource-constrained IoT nodes. Additionally, the model is optimized using TinyML techniques for real-time inference at the edge. Experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets relevant to industrial equipment and smart buildings, demonstrating that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy and low latency compared to traditional cloud-based solutions. The results confirm the framework’s effectiveness in maintaining privacy, reducing computational load, and enabling timely fault prediction in real-world scenarios. This work contributes to the advancement of intelligent, secure, and scalable maintenance strategies for next-generation IoT infrastructures.

title: What does approximation sound like? A corpus-based study of the prosody of Italian "praticamente"
abstract: This study investigates how the semantic-evaluative property of approximation can be prosodically distinguished from other pragmatic and discursive functions of the same linguistic element, focusing on the Italian adverb "praticamente". Originally meaning 'in a practical way', "praticamente" has undergone a process of pragmaticalization and now serves a range of functions, including approximator, mitigator, discourse marker, filler, and reformulator. Drawing on the corpus RadioCast-It, we adopt a corpus-based approach to statistically explore whether specific prosodic features - such as pitch, articulation rate, and duration - are significantly associated with the use of "praticamente" as an approximator vs. discourse marker. The results, obtained through a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM), reveal a systematic association between the adverb’s function and its prosodic realization: the approximator use is characterized by a faster articulation rate and lower pitch, while the discourse marker use is associated with slower articulation, higher pitch, and frequent syllable-final vowel truncation. The study provides evidence that prosody plays a key role in marking approximation, contributing to the expression of evaluative stance in spoken Italian.
